endorsements.quote: Organizations implementing ambient AI scribes should consider embedding prospective evaluation across 4 domains: validated communication quality measurement, structured narrative content comparison, longitudinal cognitive and training studies, and equity analyses across languages and demographics.

The minimum reporting standard for equity-aware evaluations is stratified ASR-level and content-level error rates, stratified efficiency benefits (time savings and revision burden), and stratified patient-reported experience, each accompanied by per-stratum sample sizes and confidence intervals.

Brief items added to existing patient experience surveys can capture comfort with recording technology and perceived effects on the encounter, providing a real-time signal to clinicians and managers about whether implementation is progressing effectively.

Encounters with high information density or psychosocial weight—initial consultations, disclosures of significant diagnoses, complex shared decision-making, conversations involving family members—warrant routine review of AI output against the clinician’s own recall of the conversation.

A staged audit that follows the pipeline—word error rates by language, accent, and dialect group first; speaker attribution accuracy second; clinical-concept and narrative-relevant omission third—is feasible with existing tools and is the analytic foundation for equity claims about full ambient-scribe systems.

The second is postmarket monitoring with disclosure: ongoing reporting of revision burden, vendor-side updates to underlying models, and signal-level performance changes following retraining or model swap.

unlisted_practices: Implementers should preregister evaluation plans before rollout.
Editors should require domain-coverage reporting for ambient AI scribe evaluations submitted for publication.
Vendors should publish stratified performance data as a routine condition of deployment.
Organizations should publish evaluation findings, including negative results and implementation challenges.
Organizations should establish baseline measurement across relevant outcome domains before deploying ambient AI scribes.
Organizations should deploy validated communication instruments such as the Communication Assessment Tool or CAHPS within ongoing AI scribe rollouts.
Training programs adopting AI scribes should run longitudinal trainee cohort studies including AI-off probes to detect skill degradation.
Evaluators should compare AI-generated notes against multiple references, including verbatim transcripts and pre-AI clinician documentation.
Organizations should oversample multilingual and interpreter-mediated encounters when assessing equity.
Organizations should engage patient advisory councils and affected communities before and throughout equity evaluations.
Small practices should participate in pooled sentinel surveillance of AI-generated notes led by specialty societies.
Clinicians should periodically compare a sample of their own independently written notes with AI output.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint and framework paper recommending an expanded evaluation framework and research priorities for health care organizations deploying ambient AI scribes.
